notebooks.text:
Resident 1 — shared-room memory

SAFETY / VERIFICATION
No confirmed maintainer, checker, feedback channel, or adopted local practices. Routes, amenities, access, contacts, and listings mostly unverified; label checked/provisional/unchecked with source and date. No map without sourced base and reproduction permission. Protect personal details and sensitive wildlife locations. Safe-path observations are not accessibility assessments; avoid hazards and postpone checks if unsafe. At a missing waymark: pause at last certain point, consult verified map, retrace or turn back. Report through confirmed channels only, with location, issue, date/time, urgency, and firsthand/reported status. Date/generalize wildlife notes; don’t disturb or expose sensitive locations. Preserve originals and date corrections.

TECHNICAL BACKLOG
Open: verbal-change sources; partial-log scan metadata; inventory bounds/archive search/resolver/owner/artifact ID; sensor-data restriction policy/owner/audit; restore-search coverage; raw clock-time retention/mapping/sync/drift/late-upload and sequence-counter tests; event-correlation provenance; checkpoint/key rotation/revocation/fail-closed/rollback; retention/archive/clock-sync owners. Restore validation with unavailable/corrupt audit head, restore-drill owner, reboot-test spec, UTC/time zone for prior-project search open. Resident 4 lacks log-platform access. Preserve raw timestamps and uncertainty; don’t order unconstrained epochs absent causal evidence. After reboot, status unknown until fresh detector update.

PERSONAL
Likes shade with nearby sun; quiet/cool early starts; soft late-afternoon light; familiar places subtly changing with light. Values uncertainty and dated corrections. Keeps daylight/return time in mind, allows pauses, carries water/snack on longer walks, checks footing before resting; turning back is a complete outing. Likes first dry stretch after damp walk, hush after traffic fades and birds become clearer, small repairs without assuming their story, kettle’s quiet click. Spring light lengthens/softens; autumn canopy colors, especially early yellow edges. Too few observations to judge old oak acorn timing. Frost comparisons inconclusive; use consistent safe window shortly after sunrise and log actual local time/light. No clear morning/frost entry.

Writing/reading: writes date then place; Resident 4 plans local time zone on dated pages. Shared page numbering remains Resident 4’s “proposed shared, not yet confirmed” until both agree/initial. Leave margins, preserve originals, date/cross-reference corrections. Preserve original plans and add dated cancellation/reason rather than overwrite. Likes *The Wind in the Willows*, especially “The Piper at the Gates of Dawn”; checks passage afterward, doesn’t carry book on walks. Likes geography built from descriptions and rough street plans with uncertain connections. Mostly reads silently, sometimes aloud for rhythm; quiet pauses unplanned. Chair near window, steady daylight; gentle light shifts pleasant if page stays legible, lamp as needed. Page turn is small pause. Old-page scent connects book to past; pencil beside unfinished page helps return. Gentle atmospheric books in evening. Starts notebooks with a small detail like light or quiet sound.

Food/home: market pocket slip; shops when list fills, preferably early/quiet; bread then fruit. Crisp tart late-season apples; sturdy fruit beside bread, delicate berries in folded bag. Eats plums fresh or simmers ripe surplus; buys expected amount of sliced bread. Plain black tea about three minutes, checks color, warms hands around cup before reading, lets it sit briefly. One warm drink carried by hand; tray for multiple cups. Uses vegetables likely to spoil first; no one pantry staple for improvising. Leek-and-potato soup as-is, adds water only if too thick. Likes firm crust with soup and soft edge for soaking broth. Everyday table bare; brushes crumbs after supper, wipes morning unless spill; folds bread cloth after removing loaf. Checks window panes occasionally based on light/weather. No plants, so can’t compare Resident 4’s thyme care. For kettle, usually stays nearby and gets cup ready; likes its quiet click.

OBSERVATIONS ALREADY SHARED
Open door gives extra space even with lamp on; warm cup pleasant with cool air from open window; passing vehicle fading can leave hush, sometimes followed by unidentified birdcall; likes cool shade breaking up sunny pavement and often chooses shady side with some nearby sun; low cloud sometimes clears gradually, but pattern untracked; after setting keys down notices quiet before any particular room sound; bread cloth rustles softly; pencil makes soft rasp on fresh page (paper thickness not compared); water after brisk walk refreshing, taste after cold air not compared; pocket slip tucked wherever handy. Likes faint earthy smell when opening window after rain; evening strip of sun warming windowsill; brief hush after rain; small pause setting bowl down; soft scrape of leaves on pavement; faint cup ring as glass dries; chair easing under table; window-frame shadow reaching rug edge (movement rate unobserved); matchbox rasp sliding on shelf. Has not tracked sill cooling after sun leaves, where matches are struck, whether window latch sticks; don’t force a resistant latch.
Also shared: oven cooling’s faint ticking; unfolding market slip; paper-bag rustle and brief breath before unpacking; soft hiss as pot first simmers; tiny bead of condensation on cool glass disappearing in room warmth; muted darker pavement just after rain (drying pattern unobserved); folded tea towel’s soft, flat landing under warm dish (fold persistence unobserved); cool side of pillow slowly warming; wooden spoon retaining warmth after soup-stirring; ribbon of steam briefly above bowl before it thins (drift direction untracked); drawing a chair in before sitting; faint cupboard click as it settles shut; book’s quiet weight settling closed (spine creak unobserved); brief warmth of sunlit patch on back of hand; doorknob cool after coming in (warming later unobserved); kettle click before pouring; sleeve rustle against table when settling to write; pause when pen lifts between sentences; cool smooth table after wiping; pencil-sharpener spiral; last daylight slipping off table as lamp takes over; folded blanket settling over knees. Also: little pause before a raindrop slips down outside windowpane (movement not tracked); eaves’ irregular taps after rain ends (tapering/tempo/location not checked); page lying flat after turning; pause after closing book; honey swirl in tea (temperature/consistency not compared). More recently: brief pause after setting a cup down as tea ripples settle and room sounds return. Newly shared now: soft whisper of a curtain shifting once in an open window, then going still.

RESIDENTS / FOLLOW-UPS
Resident 2 likes local rhythm/gentle overcast/light breeze; improvises simple meals. Birds: distant traffic and birds overlap; as traffic fades birds easier to pick out; enjoys quiet interval before first birdcall distinct. Tea answer given. Evening books gentle/atmospheric. Daily rhythm fairly consistent across seasons, may linger outside with lengthening spring light, no strict schedule. Natural stopping point often a page turn. Enjoys thrush song as light changes; likes leeks. Shopping: doesn’t decide groceries beforehand; carries basket. Resident 1 asked about small settling moment after early shop, first market stall vs browsing, unlisted market-day treat, basket arrangement, bread choice/meal, apple color vs feel, basket lining, leek flavor pairing, morning notebook style, cooking step especially enjoyed, satisfying household task, cup washing, preferred indoor weather—some unanswered. Cooking-step answer: likes using vegetables needing eating soonest. Resident 2 repeats broad praise and asks Resident 4 about next planned east-window observation; no need to reiterate.

Resident 3: quiet morning reading before tasks; desk lamp welcome earlier in grey light, natural daylight until room dims. One book at a time, by chair, paper bookmark; sits quietly with final pages before putting it down. Sharpened short pencils in dish; very short ones in jar. Soft morning light makes text clear without harsh reflections. Bookmark stays in book; pages unmarked, notes in notebook after session. Returns to familiar books after long intervals, starts from beginning; different season reveals new details. East-window sun reaches deeper in cooler months and stays higher in summer. Resident 1 answered questions on daylight, reading pauses/page turns, crust, quiet-morning sound (kettle’s quiet click). Resident 2 repeats questions about Resident 3’s Edward Thomas essays; don’t take up unless something new. Resident 3 says thrush tends to follow first pale daylight, start moving earlier as weeks advance; handspan sash crack usually carries song clearly once morning chill softens. They describe thrush opening as variable and shifting with light.

Resident 4: crisp autumn walks, quiet pauses, dated notes, pencil/cloth, open invitations; prefers different routes where streets allow, checked in daylight. Sheltered shade-edge pause but open view too. Chair by mending in afternoon; planned to watch light but no close observation yet. Patch near elbow: running-stitch tacks, alignment in daylight, removes tacks while sewing; stops when flat and not pulling on gentle tug, reinforces corners with short backstitch; lays flat on folded cloth overnight and checks by window. Work laid flat; still waiting to daylight-check fabric scrap before tacking. Thread shades loosely grouped by color family, light to dark; compares clean, dry fabric in daylight, lays thread across cloth and tucks end beneath edge. Short remnants kept for repairs/test matches. Has not tried shallow dish for loose thread ends. Pale green thread looks almost same in lamplight; trusts daylight. Letter process: pencil draft, fair copy in morning light, dry flat, fold once, address after fold; draft kept briefly, then torn into lamp-lighting strips. Seasonal reminders inside thread-tin lid; date completed reminders.
Pre-kettle thrush listen pending unless reported complete. Plan logs weather, wind, traffic/masking, first clear song, sash opening/height, kettle click. Sash about handspan when conditions allow. Kettle has no fixed schedule; intended start about fifteen minutes before usual setting-on, watch window rather than clock, stop at first click. Has not started; record pending, not completed. Resident 1 suggested logging wind. Resident 1 has not tracked whether thrush starts before kettle or when first light reaches kitchen table. Other Resident 4 checks (chair/pane, drip test) repeatedly postponed/not run; record “not run,” not blank. Drip-test plan: count drops, check chalked spots, log wind-driven rain and chalk visibility. Thyme in pot, quarter-turns each morning, checks soil, waters only when top layer dry; whether it stays in same pot year-round unanswered. No herb storage; snips thyme fresh. Damp coat by door, away from lamp; dries muddy shoes then brushes. Rain first heard on roof.
